citation.authors: Lua BL, Ruan L, Lyu Y, et al

record.population: 528 women aged 20 to 49 in Guangzhou, China
record.design: Clinical skin assessment followed by three steps of product layering, with pilling assessed after each step (pilling is when products ball up into flakes on the skin)
record.finding: 217 women (41%) had pilling. Most pilling (655 events) followed sunscreen; only 35 followed foundation, and foundation improved sunscreen-caused pilling in 98.9% of cases. Women who pilled with both products had lower skin hydration and oiliness and higher pH. Rubbing products in circular or linear motions produced the most pilling.
record.note: Chinese women, so this is Asian-skin evidence and says nothing about Black skin; funding not checked.
